Pavo cristatus.description: The Indian Peafowl is a large pheasant. The male is famous for its iridescent blue neck and long, colourful train of upper-tail coverts, which it fans during courtship displays.
Pavo cristatus.habitat: Open forests, scrub, forest edges, farmland and areas close to villages or water.
Pavo cristatus.diet: Omnivorous; feeds on seeds, grains, fruits, insects and other small animals.
Pavo cristatus.distribution: Native to the Indian subcontinent and widely found across India.

Coracias benghalensis.description: The Indian Roller is a striking blue-and-brown bird. Its bright blue wing feathers are especially visible when it flies.
Coracias benghalensis.habitat: Open country, farmland, grassland, scrub and lightly wooded landscapes.
Coracias benghalensis.diet: Mainly insects, with occasional small reptiles, amphibians and other small prey.
Coracias benghalensis.distribution: Common across much of the Indian subcontinent.

Alcedo atthis.description: The Common Kingfisher is a small, compact bird with bright blue upperparts, orange underparts and a long pointed bill used for catching small fish.
Alcedo atthis.habitat: Streams, ponds, lakes, canals and other clear waters with suitable perches.
Alcedo atthis.diet: Primarily small fish; it may also take aquatic insects and other small aquatic animals.
Alcedo atthis.distribution: Occurs across a broad range of Europe, Africa and Asia, including India.

Halcyon smyrnensis.description: The White-throated Kingfisher has a rich chestnut head and body, a white throat and breast, bright blue wings and a large red bill. It often hunts away from water too.
Halcyon smyrnensis.habitat: Farmland, gardens, wetlands, open woodland and urban areas, often near a suitable perch.
Halcyon smyrnensis.diet: Large insects, fish, frogs, lizards and other small animals.
Halcyon smyrnensis.distribution: Widespread across the Indian subcontinent and parts of western and southeastern Asia.

Psittacula krameri.description: The Rose-ringed Parakeet is a green parrot with a long tapered tail and a strong red bill. Adult males usually show a dark and pink neck ring.
Psittacula krameri.habitat: Woodland edges, parks, gardens, farmland and urban areas with trees.
Psittacula krameri.diet: Seeds, fruits, buds, flowers and cultivated grains.
Psittacula krameri.distribution: Native to parts of Africa and South Asia; widespread in India.

Pycnonotus cafer.description: The Red-vented Bulbul is a familiar crested songbird with a dark head, brown-scaled body and a distinctive red patch beneath the tail.
Pycnonotus cafer.habitat: Gardens, scrub, farmland, forest edges and towns.
Pycnonotus cafer.distribution: Common across much of the Indian subcontinent.

Acridotheres tristis.description: The Common Myna is a brown starling with a black head, yellow bill and legs, and a conspicuous yellow patch of bare skin behind the eye.
Acridotheres tristis.habitat: Town and city parks, farmland, open woodland and other human-modified habitats.
Acridotheres tristis.diet: Insects, fruit, scraps, grains and a wide range of food items.
Acridotheres tristis.distribution: Native to Asia and widespread across the Indian subcontinent.

Corvus splendens.description: The House Crow is a familiar, adaptable crow with a grey neck and breast contrasting with its darker head, wings and tail.
Corvus splendens.habitat: Villages, towns, cities, agricultural areas and coastal settlements.
Corvus splendens.diet: Omnivorous; eats insects, fruit, grains, carrion and human food waste.
Corvus splendens.distribution: Native to the Indian subcontinent and introduced in some other regions.

Eudynamys scolopaceus.description: The Asian Koel is a large cuckoo. The male is glossy black with a pale eye and greenish bill; the female is brown and heavily spotted and barred.
Eudynamys scolopaceus.habitat: Woodland, gardens, plantations and tree-rich urban areas.
Eudynamys scolopaceus.diet: Mainly fruit, especially figs and other berries.
Eudynamys scolopaceus.distribution: Occurs across South and Southeast Asia, including widely across India.

Centropus sinensis.description: The Greater Coucal is a large, ground-dwelling cuckoo with a glossy black head and body, chestnut wings and a long dark tail.
Centropus sinensis.habitat: Dense scrub, gardens, reedbeds, wetlands, plantations and forest edges.
Centropus sinensis.diet: Insects, caterpillars, snails, small reptiles, eggs and other small animals.
Centropus sinensis.distribution: Widespread in the Indian subcontinent and parts of Southeast Asia.

Spilopelia chinensis.description: The Spotted Dove is a medium-sized dove with a scaled-looking breast and a distinctive black hind-neck patch covered in white spots.
Spilopelia chinensis.habitat: Gardens, scrub, open woodland, farmland and urban neighbourhoods.
Spilopelia chinensis.diet: Mainly seeds and grains, with some small invertebrates.
Spilopelia chinensis.distribution: Widespread across South and Southeast Asia, including India.

Cinnyris asiaticus.description: The Purple Sunbird is a tiny, active nectar-feeding bird. Breeding males appear glossy dark purple, while females are olive and yellowish below.
Cinnyris asiaticus.habitat: Gardens, scrub, open woodland and flowering trees in towns and countryside.
Cinnyris asiaticus.diet: Nectar and small insects, especially when feeding young.
Cinnyris asiaticus.distribution: Common across much of the Indian subcontinent and nearby regions.
